x: Commentary on Sūrat “Wa-l-ḍuḥā”. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

By the morning brightness (1) And [by] the night when it covers with darkness (2) Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you] (3) And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life] (4) And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied (5) Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge? (6) And He found you lost and guided [you] (7) And He found you poor and made [you] self-sufficient (8)

. Our Lord, majestic is His praise, swears by the morning brightness (al-ḍuḥā), which is the whole day; and I think it is from their saying: “So-and-so was exposed to the sun (ḍaḥiya),” when he became visible
n
; and from it is His saying:
h
And that you will not be thirsty therein nor be exposed to the sun
[Ṭā Hā: 119], that is: the sun will not strike you therein. I have already mentioned the disagreement of the people of knowledge about its meaning in His saying:
h
By the sun and its brightness
[al-Shams: 1], together with the mention of our preferred view on it
n
. It has also been said: what is meant is the time of the forenoon.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: : an hour of the hours of the day

x: And His saying:
h
And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
The people of interpretation differed concerning its interpretation.
Some of them said: its meaning is: and the night when it comes on with its darkness.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
. He says: when it comes on

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar,
m: And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
. He said: when it clothes the people; when it comes

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: when it goes away.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiyah told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
. He says: when it goes away

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: when it levels out and becomes still.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us; and Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us,
m: both from Sufyān, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
. He said: when it levels out.

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
. He said: when it levels out

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
: it grew still with the creation

c: I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn,
m: he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, on His saying:
And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
: he means its settling and its stillness

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed me, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
. He said: when it grows still. He said: that is its sajw, just as the stillness of the sea is its sajw

. The most correct of these views, in my opinion, is the view of those who said: its meaning is: and the night when it grows still with its people and is fixed with its darkness, as one says: “a sājin sea,” when it is calm; and from it is the saying of Aʿshā of Banū Thaʿlabah
: “What is our fault that the sea of your cousin surged, while your sea is calm (sājin), not covering over the little worms?”
And the saying of the rajaz poet
: “How lovely is the moonlit night, and the still (sājin) night, and paths like the cloak of the weaver!”

x: And His saying:
h
Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]
. This is the answer to the oath, and its meaning is: your Lord has not abandoned you, Muḥammad, and has not hated you. It has been said:
h
nor has He detested [you]
means: nor has He detested you, the object being omitted because the hearer understands its meaning, since His saying
h
has not taken leave of you
had already preceded it; so it was known by that that the one addressed is the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiyah told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]
. He says: your Lord has not abandoned you, and has not hated you

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]
. He said: your Lord has not detested you
; has not hated you. He said: and the qālī is the one who hates

. It is mentioned that this sūrah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as God's denial of Quraysh for their saying about the Messenger of God, when the revelation was slow in coming to him: “His Lord has taken leave of Muḥammad and detested him.”

x: Mention of the report to that effect:

c: ʿAlī b. ʿAbdallāh al-Dahhān told me, he said: Mufaḍḍal b. Ṣāliḥ told us, from al-Aswad b.
m: Qays al-ʿAbdī, from Ibn ʿAbdallāh, he said

: Gabriel was slow in coming to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a woman of his household—or of his people—said: “Satan has taken leave of Muḥammad.” So God revealed to him:
Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

x: Ibn ʿAbdallāh is Jundab b. ʿAbdallāh al-Bajalī.

c: Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā al-Dāmaghānī and Muḥammad b. Hārūn al-Qaṭṭān told me, both said: Sufyān told us, from al-Aswad b.
m: Qays, that he heard Jundab al-Bajalī say: Gabriel was slow in coming to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the polytheists said: “His Lord has taken leave of Muḥammad.” So God revealed:
By the morning brightness (1) And [by] the night when it covers with darkness (2) Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, from al-Aswad b.
m: Qays, that he heard Jundab al-Bajalī say: A woman said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “I see nothing but that your companion has been slow in coming to you.” So this verse was revealed:
Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from al-Aswad b.
m: Qays, he said: I heard Jundab b. ʿAbdallāh say: A woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “I see nothing but that your devil has left you.” So there was revealed:
By the morning brightness (1) And [by] the night when it covers with darkness (2) Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

c: Ibn Abī l-Shawārib told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ziyād told us, he said: Sulaymān al-Shaybānī told us, from ʿAbdallāh b.
m: Shaddād, that Khadījah said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “I see nothing but that your Lord has detested you.” So God revealed:
By the morning brightness (1) And [by] the night when it covers with darkness (2) Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

. He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, was slow in bringing him the revelation, and some people—and they were in Mecca at that time—said: “We see nothing but that your companion has detested you and taken leave of you.” So God revealed what you hear:
Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]
. He said: Gabriel was slow in coming to him, and the polytheists said: “His Lord has detested him and taken leave of him.” So God revealed:
Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

c: I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn,
m: he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, on His saying:
Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]
: Gabriel stayed away from Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists said: “His Lord has taken leave of him and detested him.” So God revealed this verse

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

. He said: When the Qurʾān came down to him, Gabriel was slow in coming to him for some days, and he was reproached for it, and the polytheists said: “His Lord has taken leave of him and detested him.” So God revealed:
Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Hishām b.
m: ʿUrwah, from his father, he said: Gabriel was slow in coming to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was greatly distressed, and Khadījah said: “I think your Lord has detested you, from the distress I see in you.” He said: So there was revealed:
By the morning brightness (1) And [by] the night when it covers with darkness (2) Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]

x: And His saying:
h
And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life]

. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: and the Abode of the Hereafter, and what God has prepared for you in it, is better for you than the abode of this world and what is in it. He says: so do not grieve over what has escaped you of it, for what you have with God is better for you than it.
And His saying:
h
And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied
. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: and your Lord is going to give you, Muḥammad, in the Hereafter from the abundance of His favours, until you are satisfied.
The people of knowledge differed about what He promised him of giving; some of them said:

c: it is what Mūsā b. Sahl al-Ramlī told me, he said: ʿAmr b. Hāshim told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Awzāʿī relating, from Ismāʿīl b. ʿUbaydallāh b. Abī l-Muhājir al-Makhzūmī, from ʿAlī b. ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAbbās, from his father, he said: There was shown to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what would be opened up for his community after him, town by town, and he was delighted by it, so God revealed:
And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied
. So He gave him in Paradise a thousand palaces, in each palace whatever is fitting of spouses and servants

c: Muḥammad b. Khalaf al-ʿAsqalānī told me, he said: Rawwād b. al-Jarrāḥ told us, from al-Awzāʿī, from Ismāʿīl b.
m: ʿUbaydallāh, from ʿAlī b. ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAbbās, on His saying:
And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied
. He said: a thousand palaces of pearl, their soil musk, and in them whatever makes them fit [for dwelling]

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied
: and that is on the Day of Resurrection

c: Others said on this what ʿAbbād b. Yaʿqūb told me, he said: al-Ḥakam b. Ẓuhayr told us, from al-Suddī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied
. He said: Part of Muḥammad's satisfaction, may God bless him and grant him peace, is that none of the people of his household enters the Fire

x: And His saying:
h
Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge?

. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says, enumerating to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, His favours upon him and reminding him of His kindnesses toward him: Did your Lord not find you, Muḥammad, an orphan, and give you refuge? He says: so He made for you a shelter to which you take refuge, and a dwelling in which you dwell;
h
And He found you lost and guided [you]
: and He found you not upon what you are upon today.

c: Al-Suddī said on this what Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us,
m: And He found you lost and guided [you]
. He said: he was upon the way of his people for forty years. It has also been said: what is meant is: and He found you among a people gone astray, and guided you.

x: And His saying:
h
And He found you poor and made [you] self-sufficient
and He found you poor and enriched you. From it one says: “So-and-so was poor (ʿāla), he is in want (yaʿīlu ʿaylatan),” and that is when he becomes poor; and from it is the saying of the poet
n
: “The poor man does not know when his wealth will come, and the rich man does not know when he will become poor (yaʿīl).”
He means: when he will become poor.
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān:
m: : poor. It is mentioned that in the muṣḥaf of ʿAbdallāh it is: “And He found you destitute and gave you refuge”

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge? (6) And He found you lost and guided [you] (7) And He found you poor and made [you] self-sufficient
. He said: These were the stations of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before God, glory be to Him, sent him [as a prophet]

x: On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him] (9) And as for the petitioner, do not repel [him] (10) And as for the favour of your Lord, speak [of it] (11)
. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
So as for the orphan
, Muḥammad,
h
do not oppress [him]
. He says: do not wrong him, taking away his right out of regarding him as weak.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him]

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid:
m: So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him]
. He said: do not slight him and despise him. It is mentioned that this is, in the muṣḥaf of ʿAbdallāh: “do not scowl (lā takhar)”

x: And His saying:
h
And as for the petitioner, do not repel [him]
. He says: and as for whoever asks you, of the needy, do not drive him away, but feed him and fulfil his need;
h
And as for the favour of your Lord, speak [of it]
. He says: mention it.
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm told me, he said: Hushaym told us, from Abū Bishr, from Mujāhid,

x: His saying:
h
And as for the favour of your Lord, speak [of it]
. He said: [it means] prophethood
n

c: Yaʿqūb told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayyah told us, he said: Saʿīd b. Iyās al-Jurayrī told us, from Abū Naḍrah, he said:
m: The Muslims used to hold that part of giving thanks for blessings is to speak of them
. End of the commentary on Sūrat “Wa-l-ḍuḥā”; and to God belong praise and thanks.

notes.en: Ahmad (4/312), al-Bukhari (no. 4950), Muslim (1797/115), al-Tabarani (no. 1711), and al-Bayhaqi (3/14; al-Dalaʾil 7/59) transmitted it through al-Aswad ibn Qays. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/360) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dalaʾil.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 4/ 312، والبخارى (4950)، ومسلم (1797/ 115)، والطبراني (1711)، والبيهقى 3/ 14، وفى الدلائل 7/ 59، من طريق الأسود بن قيس به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 360 إلى عبد بن حميد وأبي نعيم في الدلائل.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (2/379), al-Humaydi (no. 777), Muslim (1797/114), al-Tirmidhi (no. 3345), and al-Tabarani (no. 1712) transmitted it through Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 379، والحميدى (777)، ومسلم (1797/ 114)، والترمذى (3345)، والطبراني (1712)، من طريق سفيان بن عيينة به.

notes.en: Muslim transmitted it (no. 1797) from Ibn al-Muthanna. Ahmad (4/312), al-Bukhari (no. 4951), and Muslim (no. 1797) transmitted it through Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar; al-Nasaʾi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 11681) and al-Tabarani (no. 1710) transmitted it through Shuʿba.
notes.ar: أخرجه مسلم (1797) عن ابن المثنى به، وأحمد 4/ 312، والبخارى (4951)، ومسلم (1797) من طريق محمد بن جعفر به، والنسائى في الكبرى (11681)، والطبراني (1710) من طريق شعبة به.

notes.en: Ahmad (4/312–313), al-Bukhari (nos. 1124, 1125, 4983), Muslim (no. 1797), Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir—as cited in Ibn Kathir’s Tafsir (8/446)—Ibn Hibban (nos. 6565–6566), al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 337), al-Tabarani (no. 1709), and al-Bayhaqi (3/14; al-Dalaʾil 7/58) transmitted it through Sufyan al-Thawri.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 4/ 312، 313، والبخارى (1124، 1125، 4983)، ومسلم (1797)، وابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 8/ 446 - وابن حبان (6565، 6566)، والواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 337، والطبراني (1709)، والبيهقى 3/ 14، وفى الدلائل 7/ 58، من طريق سفيان الثورى به.

notes.en: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/446) from the author. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/360) to the author.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 446 عن المصنف، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 360 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/379) from Maʿmar with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 379 عن معمر به.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/360) to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 360 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it—as cited in al-Zaylaʿi’s takhrij of al-Kashshaf (4/228)—through Muhammad ibn Saʿd with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/360) to the author.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن مردويه - كما في تخريج الزيلعي للكشاف 4/ 228 - من طريق محمد بن سعد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 360 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Al-Wahidi transmitted it in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 337) through Hisham with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/360) to Ibn al-Mundhir. Al-Hakim (2/610–611) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalaʾil (7/60) also transmitted it through Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from Khadija. Al-Suyuti attributed that report in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/360) to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه الواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 337 من طريق هشام به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 360 إلى ابن المنذر. كما أخرجه الحاكم 2/ 610، 611، والبيهقي في الدلائل 7/ 60 من طريق هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، عن خديجة، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 360 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Al-Tabarani transmitted it (no. 10650; al-Awsat, no. 3209) through ʿAmr ibn Hashim with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/361) to Ibn Abi Hatim, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dalaʾil.
notes.ar: أخرجه الطبراني (10650)، وفى الأوسط (3209)، من طريق عمرو بن هاشم به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 361 إلى ابن أبي حاتم وعبد بن حميد وابن مردويه وأبي نعيم في الدلائل.

notes.en: Ibn Abi Shayba (13/104), al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 338), and al-Hakim (2/526) transmitted it through Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah. Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Dalaʾil (7/61) through al-Awzaʿi as a report raised to the Prophet; al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (no. 572) transmitted it through Ismaʿil ibn ʿUbaydullah as a report raised to the Prophet.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 104، والواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 338، والحاكم 2/ 526 من طريق رواد بن الجراح به، وأخرجه البيهقى في الدلائل 7/ 61 من طريق الأوزاعي به مرفوعًا، والطبراني في الأوسط (572) من طريق إسماعيل بن عبيد الله به مرفوعًا.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/361) to the author, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 361 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد، وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/361) to the author. Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Shuʿab (no. 1445) through Saʿid ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbas.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 361 إلى المصنف، وأخرجه البيهقى في الشعب (1445) من طريق سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس.

notes.en: Manuscript M omits it. This chain has appeared several times earlier.
notes.ar: سقط من: م. وقد تقدم هذا الإسناد مرارًا.

notes.en: The source references were given earlier at 6/376.
notes.ar: تقدم في 6/ 376.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/362) to the author. This is an anomalous reading because it conflicts with the written form of the codex.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 362 إلى المصنف، وهى قراءة شاذة؛ لمخالفتها رسم المصحف.

notes.en: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/448) from the author and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 448 عن المصنف وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/362) to the author, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 362 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/362) to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. This is an anomalous reading because it conflicts with the written form of the codex.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 362 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم. وهى قراءة شاذة، لمخالفتها رسم المصحف.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/362) to the author, Saʿid ibn Mansur, and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 362 إلى المصنف وسعيد بن منصور وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/449) from the author. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/362) to the author.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 449 عن المصنف، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 362 إلى المصنف.
